facts.fact: A Cairo University ethnographic study of Omrania family health centre, Giza, observed between September 2016 and December 2019, states that the centre's patient records were paper family files fetched by a clerk and handed to the physician, with a paper booklet for patients without a file, very poor technology infrastructure and no connection between departments; it says more widely that Egypt's newly launched family health centres run on paper-based family records. The centre serves about 200 patients a day in a catchment of 58,639 people; one centre was studied.

systems.owner: Ministry of Health and Population family health centres
systems.tiers: Family health centres (primary care); observed at Omrania family health centre, Giza

systems.country_label: National heath registration system (2016 census of catchment population)

note: The paper's electronic record is a proposed model for the centre, untested and not implemented, so it is not entered as a system and gives no fact. The paper statement covers one primary centre directly and family health centres generally; it says nothing of hospitals, so no tiers or clinics fact is recorded.
